nodes.label: plates
nodes.comment: One set of continents shared by every climate zone — the point of this world is that the same terrain reads utterly differently at each latitude.

nodes.label: warp x
nodes.comment: East-west displacement for the warp that bends plate edges into coastlines.

nodes.label: warp y
nodes.comment: North-south displacement at a slightly different scale so the axes stay independent.

nodes.label: warped plates
nodes.comment: Plate bisectors become headlands, bays and island arcs.

nodes.label: belt mask
nodes.comment: The curve as a switch: pivoted above continental crust, it is 1 inside uplift belts and 0 elsewhere — the mask that confines the ridged noise to the ranges.

nodes.label: ridges
nodes.comment: Sharp-crested noise for the mountain belts, masked below so the plains stay smooth.

nodes.label: ranges in the belts
nodes.comment: Jagged relief only where the belt mask allows. These peaks matter later: altitude cools them below the polar cut, so snowcaps appear at any latitude without a single snow-line knob.

nodes.label: rolling detail
nodes.comment: The unremarkable hills everywhere else.

nodes.label: rolling relief
nodes.comment: A light unmasked pass so the lowlands are textured, not flat.

nodes.label: basins & platform
nodes.comment: Deep ocean basins, low continental platform, steep shelf between — Earth’s elevation histogram.

nodes.label: drainage
nodes.comment: Rain routed downhill over the whole world. The same drainage feeds temperate rivers, the frozen rivers under the cap, and the desert’s lifeline — climate only changes how each stretch is dressed.

nodes.label: eroded terrain
nodes.comment: The terrain everything stands on: valleys cut in proportion to the water they carry. The width-6 taper also digs the floodplains the desert farmland will later claim.

nodes.label: coast distance
nodes.comment: Shoreline distance for even-width beaches, measured on the uneroded terrain.

nodes.label: steepness
nodes.comment: Grade of the mountainsides, so every biome can trade soil for bare rock on its cliffs.

nodes.label: script: latitude
nodes.comment: The node this world hinges on, and nothing built in can make it: warmth as a function of world Y alone. The pole sits at y = −768, the equator at y = +768, so walking south is walking through climates. Every zone boundary downstream is a band of this one gradient.

nodes.label: climate wobble
nodes.comment: Weather is not a ruler: this bends the zone borders so the treeline meanders.

nodes.label: wobbled latitude
nodes.comment: A fifth of wobble is enough — the gradient must stay in charge or the zones dissolve.

nodes.label: sea level
nodes.comment: The 0.5 reference the lapse-rate subtraction below measures altitude from.

nodes.label: height above sea
nodes.comment: Clamped subtract: zero at sea and below, rising with the land. Pure altitude, no latitude.

nodes.label: temperature
nodes.comment: Latitude minus altitude — the lapse rate. This is why high ranges wear polar snow even in the warm south, with no node ever told where mountains are.

nodes.label: one
nodes.comment: A constant 1 so the next node can flip temperature into coldness.

nodes.label: coldness
nodes.comment: Region masks only test “at least”, so the cold biomes need cold to be the thing that is high. Taiga claims coldness ≥ 0.62, the cap claims ≥ 0.8.

nodes.label: temperate heartland
nodes.comment: The base coat, region unwired so it paints the whole world; the desert, taiga and cap overpaint their own latitudes on top. Snow line at 1 because snow here is climate’s job, not height’s.

nodes.label: southern desert
nodes.comment: Same terrain, hot region: the ground tile is simply sand. Rock still breaks through on the steeps, so desert ranges read as bare stone over dunes.

nodes.label: desert switch
nodes.comment: Near 1 where temperature passes the desert cut, near 0 elsewhere — a mask for the floodplain trick below.

nodes.label: carved depth
nodes.comment: Uneroded minus eroded terrain: nonzero exactly where the rivers dug, and the valley taper makes it a band around each channel, not a line on it.

nodes.label: desert floodplain
nodes.comment: The carved band gated to the hot zone — the only places a desert can farm.

nodes.label: river verges
nodes.comment: Farmland wherever the desert floodplain is deep enough: a green ribbon tracing every desert river from the mountains to the sea, painted before the river so the water flows through its fields.

nodes.label: taiga
nodes.comment: The cold belt: gravel shores instead of beaches, snow from 0.86 up, grass below for the pines to stand on. Painted before the rivers so its waterways stay open — only the cap freezes over.

nodes.label: rivers
nodes.comment: One drainage network for the whole planet, painted after the warm and cold-belt biomes but before the polar cap — so temperate and taiga rivers run open, while the cap buries its rivers under ice, which is exactly where frozen rivers belong.

nodes.label: polar cap
nodes.comment: Snow line 0 turns all land to snow, and the water tile is ice: the shallow sea freezes into pack ice while the deep stays black open water. Because temperature already subtracted altitude, this same region claims the high summits of every range on the planet.

nodes.label: river towns
nodes.comment: Mouths and confluences across every zone — trading towns in the heartland, oasis ports on the desert rivers, and the odd frozen way station in the north.

nodes.label: land switch
nodes.comment: Near 1 on land, near 0 at sea — multiplied into the climate fields so nothing spawns in the water.

nodes.label: warmth on land
nodes.comment: Temperature gated to dry ground: one mask whose bands are the warm-side habitats.

nodes.label: cold on land
nodes.comment: The same trick for the cold side, for pines, wolves and the tundra stones.

nodes.label: pine taiga
nodes.comment: A dense scatter of pines across the cold-but-not-polar band — the forest that gives the taiga its name, thinning to nothing at the tundra edge.

nodes.label: cottages
nodes.comment: Farmsteads across the mild middle band, where the climate does not fight the farmer.

nodes.label: deer
nodes.comment: The temperate herds, spanning a slightly wider band than the cottages.

nodes.label: wolves
nodes.comment: Hunting the same cold band the pines grow in, and a little beyond it into the tundra.

nodes.label: desert hares
nodes.comment: The only wildlife that thrives past the desert cut — quick, small, and sparse.

nodes.label: stones of the last thaw
nodes.comment: Standing stones on the tundra strip between taiga and cap — markers someone raised at the edge of the habitable world.
